_comment: COMPUTE-MATCHED depth vs width on scan-tiny: looping: 4 stages x 8 loops, d_model 128.
WHY THIS RUNG, after dyck1 turned out too easy. On dyck1 both arms reached
byte 1.000 on 2 of 3 seeds, so the comparison could not separate them -- the
opposite failure from the frontier, where everything sat at the chance floor.
scan-tiny is harder for a checkable reason rather than by hope:
- OUTPUT ALPHABET IS 4 SYMBOLS (J/W/L/R), not unary, so byte accuracy has a
real floor and a constant-symbol guesser scores 0.25.
- OUTPUT LENGTH VARIES 1..9 actions, set by the command: `twice` doubles one
action, `thrice` triples it, `and` concatenates. The model must emit a
specific LENGTH as well as specific symbols, so `mean_len_ratio` and
`length_exact_rate` are load-bearing. On dyck1 they were the ONLY
instruments that caught a seed scoring byte 1.000 / exact 0.000 because it
never emitted EOS -- byte accuracy alone called that a perfect run.
- THE ANSWER CANNOT BE LOOKED UP. It is `execute(command)`: parse clause
structure, expand modifiers, concatenate. No per-instance map exists to
memorize, so this rung rewards computation rather than storage. That is the
property subst-fst-fixed lacks and dyck1 has.
TRACK B IS A RULE-CLASS HOLDOUT, built into the task: Track A never emits
`thrice` and uses fewer `and` clauses; Track B does both. The per-track split is
therefore the compositional holdout that queue item 2 has been asking for and
that has never been run. Report the tracks separately -- a pooled number would
hide exactly the effect the split exists to expose.
THE PAIR, from examples/param_match.rs:
looping : n_stages 4,  max_loops 8, d_model 128, ffn 384, head_dim 16, 8 heads
= 32 block-steps/token, 919,172 params
wide    : n_stages 32, max_loops 1, d_model  64, ffn  58, head_dim 16, 4 heads
= 32 block-steps/token, 919,648 params  (+0.05%)
Uncontrolled difference, carried from the subst-fst pair: head COUNT is 8 vs 4
and cannot be matched at an 8x stage ratio. head_dim (16) IS matched. If the
wide arm wins, rule out head count before concluding anything about reuse.
CELL, deliberately matched to the dyck1 pair so the two rungs are comparable:
2000 steps (600 was shown to be short), per_cell 400, batch_size 64,
micro_bt_budget 3072 (48 rows/micro; the measured shared ceiling on this card
-- batch_size is the ACCUMULATION target and does NOT control micro size),
auto_batch FALSE because the tuner sizes each arm independently and would hand
these two different batches.
k_set [0] with k0_rate 1.0: the rule is the command language, universal and not
per-instance, so demos are not evidence for it. This isolates execution from
induction. Do not report a rule-INDUCTION result from this rung.
Run:
cargo run --example scaling_sweep -- \
research/experiments/arch-scan-looping.json depth gpu 8 \
